claims: SO links regulated generation and grid infrastructure to rising electricity demand; nuclear baseload and regulated investment can support reliability as large-load demand expands.

The causal bridge is conditional: large-load growth creates durable shareholder value only when incremental infrastructure is recoverable on acceptable terms and customer-affordability protections prevent adverse cost shifting.
Flexible-load contracting can improve utilization and resilience, but prospective demand is not equivalent to contracted load.
causalEdges: AI/data-center and broader electrification demand -> higher system load -> generation/grid investment need -> regulated capital deployment -> potential earnings growth
nuclear baseload capacity -> firm power availability -> grid reliability for high-load customers -> infrastructure utility
large-load capex without adequate cost allocation -> customer affordability pressure -> regulatory resistance -> slower/less-profitable investment recovery
substitutes: demand response and efficiency reducing incremental peak build
counterfactuals: If large-load demand fails to contract or materialize, the incremental grid-build thesis weakens even if baseline regulated utility demand remains.
If cost-allocation protections work and load becomes firm, current revenue flatness need not falsify the longer-duration infrastructure thesis.
falsifiers: persistent failure of forecast large loads to become contracted/energized
regulatory denial or material disallowance of incremental investment recovery
affordability impacts causing material project cancellations or adverse rate treatment

observedWeaknesses: Q2 earnings growth materially outpaced nearly flat operating revenue, so earnings momentum cannot by itself validate durable demand growth.
Large-load infrastructure is capital intensive and depends on regulatory recovery and customer protections.
risks: source dependence on issuer disclosures for current causal claims
contradictions: Historic load-growth narrative coexists with nearly flat quarterly operating revenue; this is material but not a present falsification because regulated earnings and load timing can diverge from quarterly revenue.
unknowns: share of forward large-load growth contractually committed
incremental capex and allowed-return economics specifically tied to large-load customers
adversarialRedTeam.improvementPath: Verify contracted-versus-prospective load and project-specific recovery/cost-allocation terms before increasing causal confidence.
failureAnalogs: utility overbuild against demand forecasts that arrive late
rate-base expansion constrained by affordability or regulatory disallowance

learning.strategy: cumulative evidence synthesis with explicit conditional causal bridge
learning.uncertaintyReduced: separated present quarterly revenue contradiction from long-duration load/capex thesis and identified exact verification path
